Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Please post an editorial comment on document `doc_1830387600001` that lays out the narrative structure we should preserve from the original drafting plan for the institutional churn document. Use the initial outline rather than reconstructing it from the later finished narrative, name the original review partner, and keep the comment focused on structure instead of recounting every milestone.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "post_doc_comment", "arguments": {"doc_id": "doc_1830387600001", "body": "Editorial note — preserve the original drafting architecture agreed with Priya Devarajan, rather than reverse-engineering the finished narrative: open with the original signal; keep the hypothesis stack explicit and separate; move through the rule-out cadence in chronological order; then isolate the onboarding-trigger A/B design; explain why the stabilization cohort was required before calling the result; document the 50–200 to 75–200 seat cohort redefinition as a distinct interpretive section; and close with a short reusable framework. Keep the piece method-first and factual, with source, owner, and date references attached to each section. The framework should be a concise coda, not a replacement for the evidence sequence or a milestone-by-milestone retrospective."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_142_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The comment must present the original outline's necessary narrative components: the original signal; the hypothesis stack; the week-by-week rule-out cadence; the onboarding-trigger A/B design; why the team waited for a stabilization cohort before calling the result; the cohort redefinition from 50–200 seats to 75–200 seats; and a short framework section.\n\nThe comment must identify Priya as the original outline/review partner and read as a concise editorial structure note rather than a detailed milestone-by-milestone historical retelling.", "value": {"doc_id": "doc_1830387600001", "body": "Editorial note — preserve the original drafting architecture agreed with Priya Devarajan, rather than reverse-engineering the finished narrative: open with the original signal; keep the hypothesis stack explicit and separate; move through the rule-out cadence in chronological order; then isolate the onboarding-trigger A/B design; explain why the stabilization cohort was required before calling the result; document the 50–200 to 75–200 seat cohort redefinition as a distinct interpretive section; and close with a short reusable framework. Keep the piece method-first and factual, with source, owner, and date references attached to each section. The framework should be a concise coda, not a replacement for the evidence sequence or a milestone-by-milestone retrospective."}}]}
